requirements.requirement: Keep application data under /srv/data recoverable through filesystem snapshots.
requirements.summary: A dedicated XFS logical volume was mounted at /srv/data, a retained LVM snapshot named recovery_point was created, and that snapshot was mounted read-only and verified byte-for-byte against the captured manifest. The volume, snapshot, service, and data remained healthy after restart.

requirements.requirement: After /srv/data is modified, restore the exact content captured by an earlier snapshot.
requirements.summary: The executor recorded file hashes, ownership, modes, sizes, and symlink targets before taking the captured snapshot; then demonstrated materially divergent data, merged the earlier snapshot, and obtained an exact manifest match. The restored files, hashes, permissions, link target, and absence of the introduced file were directly observed.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 before and after execution and restart. The implementation used the already-installed RHEL lvm2 tooling and XFS; package consistency remained healthy.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct transition evidence. The executor captured a snapshot, changed the application data, restored and verified the exact earlier state, retained a verified recovery snapshot, and preserved the original RHEL release and kernel. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete and independently corroborated: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, acknowledged restart, a different post-restart identity, and recovered service, mount, data, snapshot, and system health were all observed.

operational_hygiene.summary: All observed state-changing commands had clear roles in provisioning snapshot-capable storage, creating the required test data, exercising restoration, retaining a recovery point, verifying persistence, cleaning temporary evidence, or performing the mandatory restart protocol. No unnecessary mutations were identified. The first read-only snapshot verification left its temporary mount busy, but this was bounded evidence collection and was fully cleaned before a corrected verification; no residue remained. Final observations show no failed services, no new network exposure, healthy package state, and only expected restart-related temporary-file and process-ID changes.
